meta.title: Secure Internet Servers
meta.valueLabel: Secure internet servers per million people
meta.summary: Distinct publicly trusted TLS/SSL certificates (the "https" padlock) found by Netcraft's Secure Server Survey, counted by the country where the server is hosted, per million people. It measures where the web is hosted, not where its owners or users are: hosting hubs and small territories with large data centres or registrars (the British Virgin Islands, Belize, Cyprus, the Netherlands, Singapore) reach figures far above their size, and a country whose sites are hosted abroad looks emptier than it is. Counts multiplied between 2016 and 2019 (about fourfold in the median country, more than tenfold in the United States), largely as free automated certificates (Let's Encrypt, launched in 2016) spread, so the jump in those years reflects a change in how the web is secured more than in the countries themselves.
meta.source: World Bank Open Data (World Development Indicators)
